feedback_interpretation: R1 graph/gate has a positive exploratory point estimate but its paired interval includes no improvement; the two largest reported regressions occur in different cycle regimes and both have zero detected gate motifs. Gate absence is therefore not a sufficient structural explanation for false routing.

Fit clusters retain a true-preferred main cluster; the small 8-parent or 7/1-parent outlier groups have no clear false winners and cannot justify a new false-routing cluster. Cluster membership is not supplied as a predictor.
This is a constrained exploratory proposal after full feedback, not an independent confirmation or a claim that the new feature pair improves cost.
mechanism: Unsigned cycle structure is invariant under globally flipping variable signs and cannot by itself determine which Boolean phase is preferable. Positive-literal fraction changes with encoding direction and can provide that directional anchor. A two-level interaction can condition the sign-based choice on structural redundancy without treating zero recognized gate motifs as evidence for false.

proposal.hypothesis: Cycle redundancy may identify a useful structural context only when paired with encoding polarity. Keep graph context but replace gate-motif presence with positive-literal fraction; learn thresholds and actions exclusively on fit with the unchanged bounded cost-tree procedure.
